children: Artificial intelligence (AI) could eventually crack the cryptography protecting
(BTC), exposing a fundamental vulnerability in the world's largest cryptocurrency, Social Capital CEO Chamath Palihapitiya warned.
Palihapitiya cited AI's developing capability to solve age-old mathematical problems, including an alleged proof of the Riemann hypothesis, which has remained unsolved for 167 years.

In a post to Social Capital's research site, he explained the case. The post followed his comments on the Moonshots podcast in October, where he said crypto and Bitcoin are capped. The comment elicited a strong response, Palihapitiya wrote. "I asked my team to review my reasoning, double-check it with experts, and share a complete answer for our paid readers." he said.

The post claimed that time is the most important factor for online security. Encryption is only secure as long as it takes an infeasible amount of computing effort, using known techniques, to decrypt it, he wrote. The new math can cut that work down sharply.

He cited Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA), an encryption system invented in 1977, based on the difficulty of factorizing large numbers into primes. One of RSA's creators thought it would take 40 quadrillion years to break a 125-digit number that year, the post said. In 1994, a group of volunteers cracked a 129-digit number in eight months.
Why Bitcoin Stands Apart
Banks and messaging apps were at similar risk, Palihapitiya said. However, he argued that
because no institution backs it.
"Bitcoin is, in some sense, the most archetypal test of this risk, because Bitcoin is entirely self-enforcing via code, and nothing stands behind Bitcoin except the code that checks it," he wrote.
Bitcoin's signatures rely on elliptic curves, a math problem different from RSA's. He wrote that the old belief that new math arrives slowly "may be in the process of breaking."
In his words, "This is a period of alien mathematics." He said recent proofs are full of ideas nobody saw coming.
He said if there are quicker ways to crack today's encryption, the math behind them could surface soon. Security designers had thought that would take decades.
Does Bitcoin Have A 'Riemann Hypothesis' Solution?
Palihapitiya pointed to recent reports that AI has solved longstanding math problems. These claims are being verified.

Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic (ANT), said he had discovered a proof of the Riemann hypothesis while working with the company's AI model, Claude. The problem arises from 1859 and deals with the distribution of prime values. The proof’s Lean implementation has passed some independent checks, but formal recognition is yet to happen.
Both OpenAI and Anthropic claimed
the exponential time hypothesis last October. It's a decades-old idea about how quickly some difficult problems can be solved.

His post also cited an Anthropic report dated July 28. The company said its Claude Mythos Preview model found an attack against a weakened version of the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), one of the most widely used ciphers.
The attack was 200 to 800 times faster than the best previously known. Anthropic said it only works on seven of AES-128's 10 rounds and doesn't affect systems in use today.
A Reversal From Past Calls

The warning marks a sharp turn for Palihapitiya. In a previous report, he had described Bitcoin as "gold 2.0" and predicted that it could reach $1 million. In Moonshots episode 304, hosted by Peter Diamandis, he said that Bitcoin would eventually get hacked and go to zero.

Bitcoin’s price was down over 2% during the past 24 hours, trading around $59,902 at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC moved to ‘bullish’ from the ‘extremely bullish’ zone, as chatter around it dropped to ‘normal’ from the ‘high’ levels over the past day.
Palihapitiya said that crypto and Bitcoin are capped.
He said that time was the most important factor for online security.
He also said that banks were also at risk, but Bitcoin's risk was bigger because no institution backs it.

title: Chamath Palihapitiya Warns AI’s ‘Alien Mathematics’ Could Break Bitcoin As AI Tackles 167-Year-Old Riemann Hypothesis
